record.bible_text: Dead<WH04194> flies<WH02070> cause the ointment<WH08081> of the apothecary<WH07543><WTH8802> to send forth<WH05042><WTH8686> a stinking savour<WH0887><WTH8686>: <FI>so doth<Fi> a little<WH04592> folly<WH05531> him that is in reputation<WH03368> for wisdom<WH02451> <FI>and<Fi> honour<WH03519>. <RF>Dead...: Heb. Flies of death<Rf>
A wise man's<WH02450> heart<WH03820> <FI>is<Fi> at his right hand<WH03225>; but a fool's<WH03684> heart<WH03820> at his left<WH08040>.

Yea also, when he that is a fool<WH05530> walketh<WH01980><WTH8802> by the way<WH01870>, his wisdom<WH03820> faileth<WH02638> <FI>him<Fi> , and he saith<WH0559><WTH8804> to every one <FI>that<Fi> he <FI>is<Fi> a fool<WH05530>. <RF>his...: Heb. his heart<Rf><CM>

If the spirit<WH07307> of the ruler<WH04910><WTH8802> rise up<WH05927><WTH8799> against thee, leave<WH03240><WTH8686> not thy place<WH04725>; for yielding<WH04832> pacifieth<WH03240><WTH8686> great<WH01419> offences<WH02399>.

There is<WH03426> an evil<WH07451> <FI>which<Fi> I have seen<WH07200><WTH8804> under the sun<WH08121>, as an error<WH07684> <FI>which<Fi> proceedeth<WH03318><WTH8802> from<WH06440> the ruler<WH07989>: <RF>from: Heb. from before<Rf>
Folly<WH05529> is set<WH05414><WTH8738> in great<WH07227> dignity<WH04791>, and the rich<WH06223> sit<WH03427><WTH8799> in low place<WH08216>. <RF>in great...: Heb. in great heights<Rf>
I have seen<WH07200><WTH8804> servants<WH05650> upon horses<WH05483>, and princes<WH08269> walking<WH01980><WTH8802> as servants<WH05650> upon the earth<WH0776>.
He that diggeth<WH02658><WTH8802> a pit<WH01475> shall fall<WH05307><WTH8799> into it; and whoso breaketh<WH06555><WTH8802> an hedge<WH01447>, a serpent<WH05175> shall bite<WH05391><WTH8799> him.
Whoso removeth<WH05265><WTH8688> stones<WH068> shall be hurt<WH06087><WTH8735> therewith; <FI>and<Fi> he that cleaveth<WH01234><WTH8802> wood<WH06086> shall be endangered<WH05533><WTH8735> thereby.

If the iron<WH01270> be blunt<WH06949><WTH8765>, and he do not whet<WH07043><WTH8773> the edge<WH06440>, then must he put<WH01396><WTH8762> to more strength<WH02428>: but wisdom<WH02451> <FI>is<Fi> profitable<WH03504> to direct<WH03787><WTH8687>.
Surely the serpent<WH05175> will bite<WH05391><WTH8799> without enchantment<WH03908>; and a babbler<WH03956><WH01167> is no better<WH03504>. <RF>a babbler: Heb. the master of the tongue<Rf><CM>

The words<WH01697> of a wise man's<WH02450> mouth<WH06310> <FI>are<Fi> gracious<WH02580>; but the lips<WH08193> of a fool<WH03684> will swallow up<WH01104><WTH8762> himself. <RF>gracious: Heb. grace<Rf>

The beginning<WH08462> of the words<WH01697> of his mouth<WH06310> <FI>is<Fi> foolishness<WH05531>: and the end<WH0319> of his talk<WH06310> <FI>is<Fi> mischievous<WH07451> madness<WH01948>. <RF>his talk: Heb. his mouth<Rf>

A fool<WH05530> also is full<WH07235><WTH8686> of words<WH01697>: a man<WH0120> cannot tell<WH03045><WTH8799> what shall be; and what shall be after<WH0310> him, who can tell<WH05046><WTH8686> him? <RF>is full...: Heb. multiplieth words<Rf>
The labour<WH05999> of the foolish<WH03684> wearieth<WH03021><WTH8762> every one of them, because he knoweth<WH03045><WTH8804> not how to go<WH03212><WTH8800> to the city<WH05892>.<CM>
Woe<WH0337> to thee, O land<WH0776>, when thy king<WH04428> <FI>is<Fi> a child<WH05288>, and thy princes<WH08269> eat<WH0398><WTH8799> in the morning<WH01242>!

Blessed<WH0835> <FI>art<Fi> thou, O land<WH0776>, when thy king<WH04428> <FI>is<Fi> the son<WH01121> of nobles<WH02715>, and thy princes<WH08269> eat<WH0398><WTH8799> in due season<WH06256>, for strength<WH01369>, and not for drunkenness<WH08358>!
By much slothfulness<WH06103> the building<WH04746> decayeth<WH04355><WTH8735>; and through idleness<WH08220> of the hands<WH03027> the house<WH01004> droppeth through<WH01811><WTH8799>.

A feast<WH03899> is made<WH06213><WTH8802> for laughter<WH07814>, and wine<WH03196> maketh merry<WH08055><WTH8762><WH02416>: but money<WH03701> answereth<WH06030><WTH8799> all <FI>things<Fi> . <RF>maketh...: Heb. maketh glad the life<Rf>

Curse<WH07043><WTH8762> not the king<WH04428>, no not in thy thought<WH04093>; and curse<WH07043><WTH8762> not the rich<WH06223> in thy bedchamber<WH02315><WH04904>: for a bird<WH05775> of the air<WH08064> shall carry<WH03212><WTH8686> the voice<WH06963>, and that which hath<WH01167> wings<WH03671> shall tell<WH05046><WTH8686> the matter<WH01697>. <RF>thought: or, conscience<Rf><CM>
